Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

describe verb

also description, characterize (describe), characterise (describe)

classical

Cic. Or. 138: hominum sermōnēs mōrēsque (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 24: Quae monumenta dēscrīpsistī?

dēscrībō, dēscrībere, dēscrīpsī, dēscrīptum

verb, third conjugation

describe (in words); draw, depict

Also of drawing, as of figures in the sand (Cic. Rep. 1.17, Lewis & Short). Manuscripts often confuse it with discrībō, distribute (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • dēpingō, dēpingere, dēpīnxī, dēpictum — paint in words, portray

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Poen. 5.2.154: fōrmam verbīs (Lewis & Short); Cic. Rosc. Am. 74: vītam hujusce (Lewis & Short)

  • ēnarrō, ēnarrāre, ēnarrāvī, ēnarrātum — tell in full, describe point by point

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 364: omnem rem … ēnarrāmus ōrdine

  • dēscrīptiō, dēscrīptiōnis f. — a description

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Inv. 2.18: nōminis brevis et aperta dēscrīptiō (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • nōn potuit pictor rēctius dēscrībere ejus fōrmam

    a painter couldn’t have described his looks more exactlyPlaut. As. 402

  • omnem rem modo senī, quō pactō sē habēret, ēnarrāmus ōrdine

    we have just told the old man the whole business, how it stood, from start to finishTer. Ad. 364

See also explain, detail, story.

SourcesLewis & Short: describo · Lewis & Short: depingo · Lewis & Short: enarro · Lewis & Short: descriptio
